close_reason: false positive: matches() normalizes the issuer string with make_ascii_lowercase() before the contains() check; the stored substring IS pre-lowercased by add(); invariant is consistent
description: In deviation.rs, DeviationStore::add() normalizes IssuerDnContains to lowercase (line 544). However, DeviationScope::matches() (line 317) calls cert.tbs_certificate.issuer.to_string() and then make_ascii_lowercase() for comparison. This is correct when the scope was added via the store (normalized). But DeviationScope::matches() is a public method called directly (bypassing the store), and callers constructing DeviationScope::IssuerDnContains directly with a mixed-case string will get incorrect non-matches at runtime because the doc comment says 'Direct construction...should use a pre-lowercased string to preserve the invariant' — but this is only advisory, not enforced. The matches() method silently fails for mixed-case direct constructions. A constructor or invariant enforcement would close this gap.
title: DeviationStore::add normalizes IssuerDnContains but does not normalize the substring used in matches() — inconsistent invariant
